title: Irene Higginbotham's song and ASCAP
summary: Irene wrote a song for him; she belonged to ASCAP while he never filled in the form; he collects royalties since 1929.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I want to ask you, at that time that you were working with Red Allen - we know that you were a big star at that time, winning all the polls on the trombone - did you have anyone ever write any music for you, other people write music for you?
Didn't Irene - she wrote a song for you...
Irene wrote a song for you?
Didn't she give it to somebody else. It was supposed to be - was it Trombone Blues?
She belonged to the ASCAP. That's where I belonged.
Do you belong to ASCAP also?
I said I should be, but I didn't do that. I just didn't do it, period. ... They gave me a slip to fill out and I didn't do it...
She's collecting right now because with the movie that was just made -
Well I mean the government takes a chunk out of that.
'Goodmorning Heartache' is one of the hits.
You mentioned that. 'Give Me Your Telephone Number'...
... Sometimes you get paid in stamps... It's according to how they sell.
